thread:
jon: Quick follow-up on the toxic-client detection spike we ran. Thinking out loud: should scoring happen at the edge sidecar (fast, local) or as a central pacer service (consistent, heavier)?
li: my vote is sidecar for initial signal, central for aggregate decisions. local keeps latency down. central keeps global context for tenants.
maya: agree with li. also worried about state blowup if every sidecar keeps long histories. we should keep a bounded sliding window and an escape hatch to offload suspects to central KV.
sam: sketching a narrow interface we can use: sidecar emits compact feature vectors -> pacer responds with {score, ttl, action}. That keeps sidecars dumb.
li: example contract (pseudo):
```
POST /pacer/v1/score
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "features": [ {"ts": 1765439000, "rps": 12, "err_pct": 0.02, "kv_hits": 3}, ... ]
}
```
response:
```
{
  "score": 0.86,
  "ttl_s": 60,
  "action": "probation"  // accept | probational_throttle | hard_throttle | esc_to_ops
}
```
maya: tradeoffs:
- edge scoring: +latency, +survivability when central is down, -global view
- central scoring: +global context, +easier to tune, -added p99 on request path unless async
we probably need both: fast local heuristics + async central enrichment.
jon: can we keep the pacer off the hot path? e.g., sidecar applies local throttle using last-known verdict, then posts telemetry to pacer for re-eval. pacer returns updated TTL asynchronously.
sam: yep. sidecar flow idea: check local cache -> if miss, apply safe default (no hard throttle) and queue scoring request to pacer. on pacer response, sidecar updates cache and enforcement. minimizes tail latency.
nina (sec): couple security/ops notes:
- any tenant-level scoring must be redacted in higher-level logs. store only tenant-id hashes in non-prod telemetry.
- regulated tenants need allowlist option so we don't auto-throttle them; must be opt-in via contract.
- ensure pacer service has KMS-backed keys for signature verification if sidecars accept TTLs from central.
maya: abuse model concerns: attackers will try slow-steady exploitation to fly under thresholds. we need features that capture distributional shifts (e.g., sudden spike in short-lived high-token requests) and not just averages.
li: propose simple anomaly feature: recent_skew = p95_tokens / p50_tokens, and a burst_score = max(0, rps - baseline_rps). include those in vector. keep feature extraction CPU-light.
jon: operationally, we need a canary rollout plan. start with read-only scoring in prod for 2 weeks, then probation action for small tenant slice, then expand. also add a manual override in console.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary: pacer v0.1 -> us-west1, eu-west1; traffic slice 0.5%. will report back after 24h. :rocket:
sam: telemetry we want from day one: false-positive rate per tenant, time-to-detect, enforcement latency, p99 sidecar scoring time. add tags for model-version/config.
maya: simulation tasks: I will run a synthetic workload generator with slow-steady and bursty attackers and produce ROC curves. aim to have a threshold that keeps FP < 1% on standard tenants.
li: next steps:
- sam: draft the pacer API spec + response codes (ETA EOD)
- maya: simulation & baseline metrics (ETA 2d)
- jon: rollout playbook + console override UX (ETA 3d)
- nina (sec): compliance checklist for regulated tenants (ETA 3d)
jon: thanks all. feels like we have a path that balances latency and global fairness. will create an RFC draft after the API sketch lands.
